dedupe_keys.name: city of melbourne pedestrian counting system hourly counts since 2009

description: Hourly pedestrian counts since 2009 from sensors across central Melbourne, published on the City of Melbourne open data portal with more than 1.6 million records; the newest record read was for 25 September 2026. Each row gives the location and sensor, date, hour and pedestrian count, and hours with no passers-by are recorded as zero. Direction is not yet included in the hourly set but is in a companion dataset of per-minute counts for the past hour, and a third dataset lists sensor locations, status and directional readings. The council uses the system to see how people use city locations at different times of day and offers an online visualisation. Coverage: sensors in the City of Melbourne. Access: free download and Explore API. Licence: CC BY on the companion datasets. Caveats: sensors have moved or changed over time, which the council says must be considered when comparing counts across years. Simulation uses: observed pedestrian volumes for calibrating footfall, crowd and public space use models and for event and emergency planning. Related records: the Public Life Data Protocol.
